newsitem.title: INDIA: India police fire on crowd killing at least five.
newsitem.headline: India police fire on crowd killing at least five.

text.p: At least five people were killed and six wounded on Thursday when police fired on a crowd of irate cement workers in the central Indian state of Madhya Pradesh, authorities said.

K.K. Singh, a senior official in Satna district, said police opened fire because the mob of nearly 3,000 workers, demanding the arrest of the killers of a union leader, had gone on a rampage in Mehar town.
Police later imposed an indefinite curfew on Mehar, about 350 km (220 miles) from the state capital Bhopal.

Singh said the workers were demanding the arrest of the murderers of Ramesh Tiwari, who was killed on May 27 in Mehar. The crowd damaged property at Mehar police station before police fired in the air, then at the workers, Singh said.
"In all, 35 rounds were fired off, 25 of which were in the air," the local official said.
Vikram Verma, an opposition leader in the Madhya Pradesh assembly, said the death toll was much higher. "My information is 11 persons died while 22 were injured," he told Reuters.
Verma said police had fired in haste and he demanded a judicial probe.
